External systems (Azure DevOps, az CLI, Bifrost, Kilo) are never called for real in tests; they are faked/mocked.

items.title: Project skeleton & CI
items.description: Architect picks the stack (expected: TypeScript, zero runtime deps, built-in or dev-only test runner) and records it in ADR-0001, including the supported Kilo version range and the layout under backend/ (plugin single file, validation tooling, installers, provisioning). Senior BE creates a minimal plugin stub and one smoke test. CI releaser wires scripts/ci.sh and GitHub Actions to a green pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Given a clean checkout, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` is run, Then it exits 0 and the output shows the backend package's type-check and test steps were executed (not the 'no packages yet' path).

Given the repository, When docs/architecture/ADR-0001-tech-stack.md is read by an automated check, Then the file exists and contains sections for language/runtime, test runner, supported Kilo version range, and the zero-runtime-dependency single-file plugin constraint (FR-11).

Given the backend package, When the test suite runs, Then a smoke test imports the single plugin source file (e.g. backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts) and asserts it exports a plugin function that, when invoked with a minimal fake Kilo context, returns an object exposing a `config` hook.
Given backend/package.json, When an automated check inspects it, Then the `dependencies` field is absent or empty (only devDependencies are allowed).
Given a push or pull request to main, When the GitHub Actions CI workflow runs, Then it executes `bash scripts/ci.sh` (verifiable by a check that .github/workflows/ci.yml invokes scripts/ci.sh).
Given the plugin stub, When its `config` hook is invoked with a config object, Then it resolves without throwing and leaves the object unchanged (no-op until F-features land).

items.title: Plugin: JSONC parser
items.description: FR-4 / AC-5. Pure, exported function (e.g. `parseJsonc(text: string): unknown`) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Strips line/block comments and trailing commas outside strings, then JSON.parse. Zero runtime deps (FR-11). Not yet wired into the config hook (F-006).
acceptance_criteria: Given JSONC with `//` line comments and `/* */` block comments (including a multi-line block comment and a comment at end of file without trailing newline), When parsed, Then the result deep-equals the same document without comments.
Given JSONC with trailing commas in objects and arrays (including nested and with whitespace/comments between the comma and the closing bracket), When parsed, Then it parses to the expected object.
Given string values containing `https://host/path`, `/* not a comment */` and a literal `,}` sequence, When parsed, Then each string value is preserved exactly.

Given strings containing escaped quotes (`\"`) and escaped backslashes (a string ending in an escaped backslash, e.g. JSON source `"C:\\"`) followed by `//`, When parsed, Then string boundaries are respected and content is preserved.

Given invalid JSONC (unterminated string, unterminated block comment, or malformed JSON), When parsed, Then an Error with a descriptive message is thrown and the input text is not echoed in full in the message.

Given the Appendix A example from VISION.md, When parsed, Then provider.bifrost.options.baseURL equals `https://bifrost.yourcompany.internal/v1` and provider.bifrost.models has keys `azure/gpt-5` and `azure/gpt-5-mini`.
Given the plugin package after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0 and backend/package.json still has no runtime `dependencies`.

items.title: Plugin: {env:} and {file:} placeholder resolution
items.description: FR-5 / AC-8. Pure helper exposed as `__internals.resolvePlaceholders` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Recursively resolves `{env:VAR}` and `{file:path}` placeholders in the parsed shared config and returns `{ value, unresolved }` where `unresolved` is a list of placeholder names (never values). Environment, home directory and file reader are injectable for tests (defaults: process.env, os.homedir(), fs.readFileSync). Not yet wired into the config hook (F-006). Zero runtime deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given `{"x": "{env:SET_VAR}"}` and an injected env with SET_VAR=abc, When `__internals.resolvePlaceholders` runs, Then result.value.x equals `abc` and result.unresolved is empty.

Given `{"x": "{env:MISSING}", "y": 1}` with MISSING unset, When resolved, Then key x is absent from result.value (not present as undefined/empty), y equals 1, and result.unresolved contains exactly `env:MISSING`.
Given `{"x": "pre-{env:MISSING}-post"}` with MISSING unset, When resolved, Then x equals `pre--post` and result.unresolved contains `env:MISSING`.

Given `{"x": "{file:~/secret.txt}"}` and secret.txt containing `  s3cret\n` under an injected fake home directory, When resolved, Then x equals `s3cret` (trimmed) and the file read targeted `<home>/secret.txt` (`~/` expanded).

Given `{file:...}` that cannot be read (missing path, a directory, or a reader that throws with the file contents in its error message), When resolved, Then the key is dropped, result.unresolved contains `file:<path as written>`, and no returned or thrown value contains the file contents or the reader's error text.

Given placeholders nested in objects and arrays (e.g. `{"a":{"b":["{env:SET_VAR}","{env:MISSING}","keep"]}}`), When resolved, Then nested values follow the same rules, an array element that is only an unresolved placeholder is removed from the array (giving `["abc","keep"]`), and non-string values (numbers, booleans, null) and strings without placeholders are returned unchanged.

Given any input object, When resolved, Then the input object is not mutated, own keys `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` in the input do not pollute Object.prototype, and a string containing multiple placeholders (`{env:A}/{env:B}`) resolves each one.

Given the plugin package after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `resolvePlaceholders` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: in-place merge with defaults/enforce modes
items.description: FR-6 / AC-6 / AC-7. Pure helper exposed as `__internals.mergeConfig(target, shared, mode)` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Deep-merges the (already parsed and placeholder-resolved) shared config into Kilo's resolved config object, mutating `target` in place. Plain objects are merged recursively; arrays and scalars are leaf values whose conflict is decided by mode (`defaults`: local wins; `enforce`: shared wins); a key absent locally is added from shared in both modes. Top-level `$schema` and `plugin` in the shared config are ignored. Any `apiKey` key at any depth in the shared config is never applied (local apiKey always preserved; vision AC-6, FR-12). Values copied from shared are deep-cloned so target never aliases shared. An unrecognised mode is treated as `defaults` (conservative). Not yet wired into the config hook (F-006). Zero runtime deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given local `{model:'a'}` and shared `{model:'b', small_model:'s'}`, When `__internals.mergeConfig` runs in `defaults` mode, Then target.model equals `a` and target.small_model equals `s` (shared-only keys are added).

Given local `{model:'a', provider:{bifrost:{options:{baseURL:'L'}}}}` and shared `{model:'b', provider:{bifrost:{options:{baseURL:'S'}}}}`, When merged in `enforce` mode, Then target.model equals `b` and target.provider.bifrost.options.baseURL equals `S`; and When merged in `defaults` mode, Then both local values are kept (AC-7).

Given local `provider.bifrost.options.apiKey = 'sk-bf-local'` and a shared provider.bifrost block whose options contain `apiKey: 'sk-bf-shared'` plus `baseURL`, When merged in `defaults` and in `enforce` mode, Then apiKey still equals `sk-bf-local`, baseURL is merged per mode, and with a local config that has no apiKey the shared apiKey is not added (AC-6).

Given local keys absent from the shared file at top level and nested (e.g. `provider.other`, `provider.bifrost.options.headers`, `agent.x`), When merged in either mode, Then those keys and their values are unchanged.
Given a shared config with top-level `$schema` and `plugin`, When merged in either mode, Then the local `$schema` and `plugin` values are unchanged, and when absent locally they are not added.

Given a target object, When merged, Then the function mutates and keeps the same target reference (including existing nested object references such as target.provider), the shared input is not mutated, and mutating a nested object or array in shared after the merge does not change target.

Given arrays or type conflicts (local `instructions:['a']` vs shared `['b','c']`; local object vs shared string), When merged, Then arrays are replaced wholesale (never concatenated) and conflicts resolve by mode (`defaults` keeps local, `enforce` takes shared), and an unrecognised mode behaves as `defaults`.

Given a shared config parsed from JSON containing own keys `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype` at top level and nested, When merged, Then Object.prototype is not polluted and no such key alters target's prototype; and When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `mergeConfig` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: settings resolution (options, env, defaults)
items.description: FR-1 / FR-8 (and the settings half of FR-3). Pure helper exposed as `__internals.resolveSettings(options, deps?)` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Resolves org, project, repo, path, branch, mode, pat, timeoutMs with precedence: plugin option (non-empty string / finite number) > KILO_AZDO_* env var (KILO_AZDO_ORG, KILO_AZDO_PROJECT, KILO_AZDO_REPO, KILO_AZDO_PATH, KILO_AZDO_BRANCH, KILO_AZDO_MODE, KILO_AZDO_PAT, KILO_AZDO_TIMEOUT_MS) > built-in default (path `/kilo.jsonc`, branch `main`, mode `defaults`, timeoutMs 5000; org/project/repo/pat have no default). Returns `{ settings, missing, warnings }` where `missing` lists required setting names (org, project, repo) that are unset and `warnings` are fixed messages naming settings only, never values. Env is injectable (default process.env, own properties only). The AZDO_PAT / AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT fallback and the az token belong to F-005; logging through Kilo's logger is wired in F-006. Not yet wired into the server/config hook. Zero runtime deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given options `{org:"opt"}` and an injected env with KILO_AZDO_ORG=env, When `__internals.resolveSettings` runs, Then settings.org equals `opt`; and Given no `branch` option and KILO_AZDO_BRANCH=dev, Then settings.branch equals `dev` (option > env precedence verified for each of org, project, repo, path, branch, mode, pat, timeoutMs).

Given no options (undefined) and an empty env, When settings resolve, Then path is `/kilo.jsonc`, branch is `main`, mode is `defaults`, timeoutMs is 5000, org/project/repo/pat are undefined, and `missing` deep-equals ["org","project","repo"].

Given mode `enforce` from options or from KILO_AZDO_MODE, When settings resolve, Then mode is `enforce`; and Given an invalid mode (e.g. `force`, `ENFORCE`, a number) from options or env, When settings resolve, Then mode is `defaults` and `warnings` contains an entry naming `mode`.

Given timeoutMs 3000 as an option number, or KILO_AZDO_TIMEOUT_MS=`2500` in env, When settings resolve, Then timeoutMs is 3000 or 2500 respectively; and Given a non-numeric, zero, negative, NaN, Infinity or non-integer value (option or env), When settings resolve, Then timeoutMs is 5000 and `warnings` contains an entry naming `timeoutMs`.

Given options that are null, an array, a string or a number, or option values of the wrong type (number for org, object for branch) or empty/whitespace-only strings, When settings resolve, Then no error is thrown and each such value is ignored so the env value or default applies; string values are trimmed, and a path without a leading `/` (e.g. `teams/a/kilo.jsonc`) is normalised to `/teams/a/kilo.jsonc`.

Given a `pat` option and KILO_AZDO_PAT both set, When settings resolve, Then settings.pat equals the option value; and Given any input containing a pat value (valid or wrongly typed), When `missing`, `warnings` and any thrown error are inspected, Then none of them contains the pat value.

Given inputs, When settings resolve, Then the options object and env are not mutated, an env created via Object.create({KILO_AZDO_ORG:"inh"}) does not supply org (own properties only), and own keys `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` in options do not pollute Object.prototype or the returned settings.

Given the plugin package after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `resolveSettings` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: Azure DevOps fetch and authentication
items.description: FR-2 / FR-3 / FR-8. Async helper exposed as `__internals.fetchRemoteConfig(settings, deps?)` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Takes the output `settings` of `resolveSettings` (F-004, contract 0.5.0; `settings.pat` already covers the plugin option and KILO_AZDO_PAT) and fetches the shared file via the Azure DevOps Git Items API. Returns a discriminated result `{ ok: true, text }` or `{ ok: false, error }` where `error` is a fixed, value-free code/message (e.g. invalid-settings, auth-unavailable, timeout, http-<status>, too-large, bad-response, network); it NEVER throws or rejects (FR-10). Injectable deps: `fetch` (default globalThis.fetch), `env` (default process.env, own properties only), `runAz` (default: node:child_process execFile without a shell, bounded by timeoutMs), and timer/AbortController seams as the Architect sees fit. Request uses `Accept: application/json`; the file text is read from the JSON body's `content` string. Lone UTF-16 surrogates in settings (security low finding 1, cycle 0006) must be handled here: either an `isWellFormed()` guard via a contract amendment or catching URIError during URL building. Parsing, placeholder resolution, merge, cache and logging stay in F-006. Zero runtime npm deps (FR-11); Node built-ins only.
acceptance_criteria: Given settings {org:'my org', project:'plat form', repo:'kilo-config', path:'/teams/a b/kilo.jsonc', branch:'release/1', timeoutMs:5000} and a fake fetch, When `__internals.fetchRemoteConfig` runs, Then exactly one GET is sent to `https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_apis/git/repositories/{repo}/items` with org/project/repo percent-encoded as path segments and query parameters path, versionDescriptor.version=<branch>, versionDescriptor.versionType=branch, includeContent=true and api-version=7.1 (all values percent-encoded), with an `Accept: application/json` header; and Given a 200 response whose JSON body has `content` equal to a JSONC string, Then the result is `{ ok: true, text }` with text equal to that string byte-for-byte (not parsed).

Given PAT sources, When the request is built, Then the Authorization header is `Basic ` + base64(':' + pat) using the first available of: settings.pat (plugin option or KILO_AZDO_PAT, from resolveSettings), then injected env AZDO_PAT, then AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT (empty/whitespace-only values skipped, env read as own properties only); and in every PAT case the injected az runner is never invoked.

Given no PAT from any source, When fetching, Then the injected az runner is invoked once with arguments starting `account get-access-token --resource 499b84ac-1321-427f-aa17-267ca6975798` (no shell), the trimmed returned token is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; and Given the runner throws, exits non-zero, times out or returns empty output, Then no HTTP request is sent and the result is `{ ok: false }` with a fixed auth-unavailable error.

Given a fake fetch that never responds, When fetching with timeoutMs 50, Then the request's AbortSignal is aborted at the timeout and the result is `{ ok: false }` with a timeout error within a bounded time (no hang), and the default timeout when settings come from resolveSettings defaults is 5000 ms (FR-8).

Given a non-2xx response (e.g. 401, 404, 500), or a fetch that rejects with an error whose message contains the PAT, When fetching, Then the result is `{ ok: false }` and the error includes the HTTP status number for non-2xx responses, while no returned error contains the PAT, the bearer token, the Authorization header value or the underlying error's message.

Given a response larger than 1 MiB (declared by Content-Length or actual body length when the header is missing or lies), or a 200 body that is not JSON or lacks a string `content` field, When fetching, Then the result is `{ ok: false }` with a too-large or bad-response error and no oversized text is returned (cap enforced before any parsing; parseJsonc memory is about 50x input size).
